query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases is governed by the formation of a thermally grown oxide (TGO) layer, which leads to catastrophic failure when the TGO layer reaches a critical thickness, causing spallation and subsequent exposure of the underlying alloy to the corrosive environment.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of temperature (700-1000°C) and gas composition (air, Ar-20%O2, Ar-5%H2) to identify degradation mechanisms
generation.conditions: Exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases at elevated temperatures for 100 hours
generation.mechanism: Thermodynamic and kinetic principles governing oxidation and corrosion, including the formation of a TGO layer and its subsequent spallation
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in degradation rate relative to the starting-state baseline when exposed to air at 900°C, and a 50% decrease in degradation rate when exposed to Ar-5%H2 at 800°C
generation.baseline: Degradation rate of the alloy in the as-manufactured state
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 700-1000°C, gas composition range: air, Ar-20%O2, Ar-5%H2
generation.uncertainty: The exact critical thickness of the TGO layer leading to catastrophic failure is uncertain and may depend on the specific exposure conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled exposure of the alloy to oxidizing and reducing gases at elevated temperatures, with systematic variation of temperature and gas composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the degradation rate does not increase by at least 20% when exposed to air at 900°C, or if the TGO layer thickness does not reach a critical value of 10 μm, then the hypothesis is falsified
